title: The leap, held lightly
note: Abbas ibn Firnas is said to have glided from a height in Cordoba, a story the house holds lightly for its late written record.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-engineering (The leap of Abbas ibn Firnas): 'Abbas ibn Firnas, about 810 to 887, Cordoba.' 'built himself wings of silk and feathers, leapt from a height before a watching crowd, glided some distance, and crash landed, hurting his back.' 'six centuries before Leonardo sketched his machines.' 'the court poet Mu'min ibn Said mocked him for flying faster than the phoenix.' 'A rival's joke is not a flight log.' 'The full account appears in al-Maqqari, writing about seven hundred years later.'
research.retell: An inventor named Abbas ibn Firnas may have glided through the air on homemade wings six hundred years before anyone else tried, but the only evidence from his own time is a rival's mocking joke, and the full story was not written down until centuries later.

lines.text: A man tried to fly six centuries early
lines.sub: six hundred years before Leonardo's wings
an inventor named Abbas ibn Firnas leaps

lines.text: He builds wings of silk and feathers
He leaps from a height before a crowd
He glides some distance through the air
Then he lands hard, hurting his back
Only a rival's joke survives from his time
lines.sub: the full tale was written centuries later

lines.text: A rival's joke is not a flight log
lines.sub: a poet mocked him for flying like a bird

lines.text: We hold this story lightly, not proven
